Smoothing
Temporal averaging

Fast responds quickest, Slow is a steadier average, and Inf keeps a running average until Reset averaging. Switch Settings mode to Advanced for the full 1–10 scale.

1–3 are FIFO averages of 2, 4 or 8 FFT analysis frames; the oldest frame drops out as a new one arrives. 4–10 are frequency-weighted: lows average longer than highs. 6 is the recommended general starting point; Inf keeps a running average until Reset averaging.

A setup stores banding, scales, display, the target curve, zoom, markers, trims, channel mode and the EQ export options — everything about how you measure, not the measurements themselves. Traces are saved separately.

Input

Input 2 trim

Mirrors whatever the OS exposes: built-in mic, headset, or a USB audio interface. 1+2 measures both channels of a stereo interface at once — a measurement mic on input 1 against a console feed on input 2 — and overlays them on the RTA. Each plot can follow either input, and each input keeps its own trim. A mono input shows the same signal on both.

Data
EQ reference
EQ smoothing
EQ file layout

The 31-band file is one gain per ISO third-octave centre (20 Hz – 20 kHz), clamped to ±12 dB and rounded to 0.5 dB — the range a graphic EQ can actually take. With a target curve shown the gains correct towards it; without one they correct towards the 500 Hz – 2 kHz average, so the house curve is left alone.

About

Two-input real-time analyzer: fractional-octave RTA, spectrograph with rewind, 1+2 input overlay, draggable A/B frequency markers with zoom to the selection, captured traces with spatial averaging, and target curves for FOH, monitors, cars and listening rooms. Levels are relative full-scale (dBFS); this build has no SPL metering and no calibrated absolute levels. Independent implementation — not affiliated with, or endorsed by, Rational Acoustics. Overlaid inputs are two independent RTAs: there is no transfer function, no impulse response and no .srf interchange.
